doc.title: Wayne Andre interviewed by Monk Rowe, New York City, New York, January 7, 2002

chapter: Childhood, Berklee and the Air Force
title: Studying at the Schillinger House
summary: He auditioned in Boston at 17, won a full scholarship, and left after a year to go on the road.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: School days: grades, teachers and leaving school

blocks.x: And I see you did some study at the Schillinger House?
I’ve seen that name come up a lot.
You see it come up a lot?
Because not many people know the name.
But that’s what it was called when I went there. It’s now the Berklee School of Music.

Yeah, it’s interesting. Because my mother took me up to Boston, I was 17 years old, and I auditioned for this fellow Ken McKillup, who was like the assistant to Larry Berk. And they gave me a full scholarship. And I can’t remember the details. I had a full scholarship. I didn’t pay any tuition, based on my audition I guess, and I don’t know if that would have applied to the second, third or fourth year of the school or not but once I got out of the school the first year I ended up going on the road and I never went back you know. I mean it’s one of those things.
